page: Microsoft Azure NC80adis_H100_v5 is an isolated, GPU-accelerated virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 80 dedicated virtual CPUs backed by 640.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It supports Azure Premium Storage and is structured for computationally intensive workloads that demand isolated hardware resources.

Hardware acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs delivering a combined 188 GB of high-bandwidth video memory. For local data caching, temporary processing, and scratch storage, the instance integrates 7,955 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The combination of dense host memory, direct dual-GPU processing capacity, and multi-terabyte solid-state storage minimizes external I/O bottlenecks during distributed compute operations.

Given its hardware profile, NC80adis_H100_v5 delivers high resource density for workloads requiring massive GPU acceleration paired with extensive memory and local disk bandwidth. It is tailored for artificial intelligence model training, large language model inference, molecular modeling, and complex simulations. Qualitative cost efficiency depends on sustained high utilization of both its specialized accelerator hardware and large integrated NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure NC80adis_H100_v5 is an isolated, GPU-accelerated server instance designed for compute-intensive machine learning and scientific workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD processor on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 80 dedicated vCPUs paired with 640.0 GB of system memory, equating to 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs with a collective 188 GB of VRAM, supported by 7,955 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The substantial local disk footprint and high GPU memory volume facilitate intensive data manipulation, rapid checkpointing, and large-scale model execution without reliance on remote storage transfers. This configuration is tailored for deep learning training, large language model inference, batch processing of heavy datasets, and complex numerical simulations where concurrent accelerator access and rapid local I/O are necessary.
